Solve for the intervention achieving a target value

Source: R/solve-alpha.R
solve_alpha.Rd

Finds the intensity intervention alpha at which the estimate returned by fun(alpha) equals theta, assuming the estimate is increasing in alpha. The search first expands a bracket around the solution, then narrows it by secant steps (with bisection as a fallback), caching evaluations of fun along the way.

Usage

solve_alpha(
  fun,
  theta,
  c_n,
  alpha_init = 1,
  expand_up = 2,
  expand_down = 0.25,
  max_iter = 100,
  alpha_min = 0.001,
  alpha_max = 100,
  verbose = FALSE,
  trace_every = 1L
)

Arguments

fun

A function of alpha returning a list with elements estimate (a named vector containing tmle_est or one_step_est, and se) and eic, such as a call to tmle_alpha().

theta

Number. The target value of the estimate.

c_n

Positive number. Tolerance; the search stops once the estimate is within c_n of theta.

alpha_init

Number. Starting value of alpha.

expand_up

Number greater than 1. Factor by which alpha is multiplied while searching upwards for a bracket.

expand_down

Number between 0 and 1. Factor by which alpha is multiplied while searching downwards for a bracket.

max_iter

Positive integer. Maximum number of steps in each of the bracketing and narrowing phases.

alpha_min, alpha_max

Numbers with 0 < alpha_min < alpha_max. Bounds on alpha.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print progress every trace_every evaluations.

trace_every

Positive integer. How often to print progress when verbose = TRUE.

Value

A list with elements alpha_hat (the best alpha found), converged (whether it is within c_n of theta), dist (its distance to theta), c_n, grid (a data frame of all evaluated alpha, psi and se) and eic (the influence curve at alpha_hat).

Details

This solves the calibration equation of Rytgaard and van der Laan, and is used by calibrate_alpha().

Examples

# psi(alpha) = 0.6 * (1 - exp(-alpha)) has a known inverse, so
# solve_alpha() should recover alpha = -log(1 - 0.3 / 0.6).
fun <- function(alpha) {
  psi <- 0.6 * (1 - exp(-alpha))
  list(estimate = c(tmle_est = psi, se = 0.01), eic = rep(0, 10))
}
res <- solve_alpha(fun, theta = 0.3, c_n = 1e-6)
res$alpha_hat
#> [1] 0.6931482
-log(1 - 0.3 / 0.6)
#> [1] 0.6931472
